STATUS: COMPLETE

**Assessment of search-indexer outage:**

- **Service:** search-indexer — owned by the **discovery** team, **tier 3**. On-call: discovery-oncall@northwind.example.
- **Severity:** S3 — matched matrix row *"limited or single-user impact, or a tier-3 service."* Even though the impact here is total failure across all cluster nodes, search-indexer is a tier-3 service, so the tier-3 row applies.
- **Has this happened before?** Not exactly. The closest recorded incident is **INC-1877** ("Index lag over 20 minutes"), where a burst reindex job starved the worker pool and caused stale search results — but that was degradation/lag, not a complete failure of all indexing jobs. There is no prior incident on record of search-indexer being fully down with 100% job failure, so this appears to be a new failure mode. Note INC-1877's root cause (worker-pool starvation from a reindex job) may still be a useful starting hypothesis if a reindex was recently triggered.

Suggested next step: page discovery-oncall and check whether any recent reindex or deployment preceded the failure.

Customer note:
**Search indexing outage**

Search indexing is currently down — every indexing job across the search cluster is failing, so new content will not show up in search results until this is resolved. This is a new kind of failure for us; past problems only caused slower or outdated search results, never a complete stop. Engineers are investigating, including checking whether a recent update or reindexing task triggered it. We'll share updates as we learn more.
